claims.text: In solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn, strain-rate-induced adiabatic heating triggers dynamic recrystallization.
Dynamic recrystallization promotes the formation of localized adiabatic shear bands.
Competition between strain-rate hardening and heat softening governs the strength–ductility balance of FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes.
The starting FeNiCrMn alloy has a homogeneous as-solidified microstructure without major preexisting defects or processing-induced heterogeneity.
The study will compare compression behavior from approximately 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
The study will span sub-ambient to moderately elevated environmental temperatures.
Environmental temperature and strain rate will be varied independently while sample preparation is held constant.
The relevant structural mediator is dynamically recrystallized material within adiabatic shear bands.
At high strain rates, localized adiabatic heating creates dynamically recrystallized zones that develop into adiabatic shear bands.
Adiabatic shear bands initially enhance strain-rate hardening and thereby increase yield strength.
Beyond a threshold strain rate, excessive local heating produces thermal softening and a drop or inflection in strength.
Yield strength will increase with strain rate up to a point and then decrease or show an inflection associated with thermal softening or earlier failure.
The predicted strength inflection or earlier failure will occur concomitantly with observable dynamic recrystallization and adiabatic shear-band formation.
At low strain rates and moderate temperatures, FeNiCrMn exhibits strain-rate hardening without significant localized dynamic recrystallization or adiabatic shear bands.
The proposed mechanism is limited to as-solidified FeNiCrMn within the studied temperature and strain-rate range.
Significant processing-induced defects, substantial compositional changes, or temperatures beyond phase stability may invalidate the mechanism.
Localized heating, recrystallized grain structure, shear bands, yield strength, and compressive strength can be measured and correlated in the proposed tests.
Absence of dynamic recrystallization or shear bands at high strain rates, or absence of the predicted nonlinear mechanical response, would falsify the hypothesis.
